ethics_check.title: Ethics Approval Check
ethics_check.summary_text: All papers that appeared to involve live data collection contained an ethics approval statement.

table.text: The study was approved by the University of California San Francisco (UCSF) Institutional Review Board [24-41224], and KnowCKD participants provided written informed consent.

No additional inclusion or exclusion criteria were applied Participants took part in 3 sequential video-based discussion sessions and provided feedback on message content, terminology, communication strategies, and questionnaire design.
Participants were adults receiving primary care at a single academic medical center with documented hypertension, without diabetes, and without albuminuria testing during the preceding 12 months.

Eligible participants were also required to use MyChart, have access to a smartphone, and have an upcoming primary care appointment scheduled at least 1 week after enrollment, allowing sufficient time for delivery of KnowCKD before the clinical encounter.

Potentially eligible participants were identified through a UCSF EHR-based recruitment service that conducted daily searches of primary care schedules and sent electronic invitations to patients meeting initial study criteria.
Following enrollment, KnowCKD participants completed the pre-intervention questionnaire and received the intervention through the Eureka digital research platform.
Participants completed a questionnaire before receiving KnowCKD and a follow-up questionnaire after their primary care visit.
Following exposure to KnowCKD and the associated primary care visit, 8 participants took part in a single 60-minute facilitated focus group.
To minimize recall bias, recruitment was restricted to participants enrolled in KnowCKD during 2026.
Participants were recruited from survey respondents who had indicated willingness to be contacted for further research.

KnowCKD participants were matched to up to 2 contemporaneous controls using greedy nearest-neighbor matching without replacement, with a caliper of 0.2 times the standard deviation of the logit propensity score.
Based on the preintervention questionnaire, participants had a mean age of 60.0 years, 54.4% were female, and 57.9% identified as White.
Eight participants enrolled during 2026 participated in the post-intervention focus group.
Nevertheless, later completion among participants enrolled near the end of the study may not have been captured.

Fifth, the qualitative evaluation consisted of a single focus group restricted to participants enrolled during 2026 to minimize recall bias and was intended to characterize experiences and implementation considerations rather than estimate the prevalence of specific perspectives.
The study was approved by the University of California San Francisco (UCSF) Institutional Review Board [24-41224], and KnowCKD participants provided written informed consent.

power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::
